00262.comparison: Concurrent versus sequential tamoxifen with four EC75 cycles.
00262.applicability: NCCP EC90 cites this trial, but epirubicin was75mg/m², not90mg/m². It tested tamoxifen timing, not the incremental benefit of EC90.

endpoints.metric: No matched numerical EC90 benefit estimate
endpoints.interpretation: Do not transfer this result to an EC90-versus-alternative benefit claim.
endpoints.result_text: No statistically established DFS advantage for either tamoxifen-timing strategy.

00262.qualitative_result: The regimen source establishes EC90 use; the cited trial does not quantify the benefit of its90mg/m² dose.
00262.harms: Anthracycline cardiac injury, myelosuppression and fertility effects remain relevant; different doses cannot be assumed equivalent.

00263.population: 705 patients receiving first-line chemotherapy for metastatic breast cancer
00263.comparison: EC75/600 versus epirubicin75/paclitaxel200 every3weeks, at most6cycles in the trial.

Median differences are not individual added lifespan.

00265.population: 565 patients with poor-prognosis node-positive early breast cancer
00265.comparison: Adjuvant FEC100 versus FEC50, six21-day cycles.
00265.applicability: Dose and adjuvant schedule match. This trial does not establish neoadjuvant pCR or compare FEC with contemporary taxane/targeted strategies.

00269.population: 456 randomised metastatic patients;390 evaluable for efficacy
00269.comparison: FEC100 versus FEC50 every21days, up to6cycles (8for complete response).
00269.applicability: Metastatic FEC50 dose matches. Trial course limits differ from NCCP continuation criteria.

00423.comparison: AT50/75 versus AC60/600 every21days; up to8cycles in the trial.
00423.applicability: AT doses match; NCCP specifies6cycles. Metastatic trial results are not an isolated estimate for locally advanced treatment.

endpoints.interpretation: Longer TTP with AT (P=.014). TTP is not interchangeable with PFS.

endpoints.result_text: Overall survival was comparable between groups.

00423.qualitative_result: Improved response and TTP must be weighed against toxicity.
00423.harms: Febrile neutropenia occurred in33% withAT versus10% withAC; G-CSF and fitness review matter.
limitations: Historical first-line chemotherapy population; modern receptor-directed options require review.
Trial8-cycle maximum differs from NCCP6-cycle course.

00260.population: 4,954 eligible women with stageII–III operable breast cancer
00260.comparison: After fourAC cycles: weekly paclitaxel versus paclitaxel every3weeks; other docetaxel arms also studied.
00260.applicability: Supports the weekly taxane schedule afterAC. Trial randomised taxane type/schedule, not the contribution of AC or neoadjuvant use.

endpoints.interpretation: Lower DFS-event hazard in this arm comparison.
No statistically significant OS difference at long-term follow-up.

00260.qualitative_result: The factorial primary comparisons and individual arm contrasts answer different questions; avoid a blanket claim that weekly treatment improves every endpoint.
00260.harms: Weekly paclitaxel can cause cumulative neuropathy; review symptoms before each dose.

00278.population: 1,973 patients with node-positive early breast cancer
00278.comparison: Dose-dense every2weeks versus conventional every3weeks, pooled across concurrent/sequential schedules.
00278.applicability: Supports dose density; pooled factorial comparison is not solely the precise00278sequence.

endpoints.interpretation: Lower DFS-event hazard with dose-dense treatment.
Lower death hazard with dose-dense treatment.

00278.qualitative_result: Benefit persisted at long-term review. Relative hazards are not absolute percentage-point gains.

00432.population: 4,046 patients with HER2-positive operable breast cancer
00432.applicability: Supports adding trastuzumab to the whole adjuvant strategy. Trial taxane schedules differed; not an isolated estimate for maintenance alone or preoperative response.
00432.qualitative_result: Do not attribute the whole strategy benefit solely to continuation after paclitaxel.
00432.harms: Cardiac toxicity is a key trade-off, particularly after anthracyclines; surveillance continues after chemotherapy.
limitations: Historical adjuvant population before contemporary dualHER2 and response-adapted postoperative options.
No concurrent AC/trastuzumab benefit is inferred.
